voucher_rent_ceiling.what_this_is: the range a PHA's voucher payment standard can be set to (90-110% of the Small Area FMR for this ZIP). It is a ceiling on gross rent (rent + tenant-paid utilities), not a promised rent: the PHA also caps rent at local comparable unassisted rents (rent reasonableness) and subtracts tenant-paid utilities. The voucher pays for the smaller of the family's voucher size and the unit's bedrooms, so extra bedrooms earn nothing.
voucher_rent_ceiling.policy_2026: HUD's 2026 Budget Management Letter pushes PHAs to cut payment standards toward the lower end of the range and to end exception payment standards; plan on the low figure.
voucher_rent_ceiling.year_note: HUD FMR/SAFMR values as stored in meta.rent (HUD eGIS layer vintage). FY2027 values took effect 2026-10-01 and may differ: confirm at https://www.huduser.gov/portal/datasets/fmr.html

assistance.occupancy_by_bedrooms: up to 2 persons at 2 per bedroom (typical PHA subsidy standard)

checklist.why: 1 bedroom(s) (estimated from LiDAR footprint & stories). PHAs size vouchers at about 2 persons per bedroom; a bedroom must be a sleeping room with a window (HQS) and usually an openable egress window and a door. Extra bedrooms beyond the voucher size earn no extra subsidy. footprint 50 m2 x 1 stories (LiDAR height estimate) x 0.8 = ~40 m2 living area; conservative, capped at 4.

Gross rent (rent + tenant-paid utilities) must be at or below the PHA payment standard, about $1,854-$2,266/month here for 1BR, and no higher than comparable unassisted rents. We do not estimate a rent for this house. Context only: at the low ceiling, 12 months of gross rent = 5.3% of the $417,000 estimated value (ACS ACS 5-year 2020-2024 tract median value x FHFA ZIP 32803 HPI 2024->2025).
year built unknown; if before 1978 and a child under 6 will live there the Lead-Safe Housing Rule applies

NSPIRE: smoke alarm on every level, inside each bedroom and within 21 ft of each bedroom door; carbon-monoxide alarms where there are fuel-burning appliances or an attached garage. Not visible in any dataset.
a permanently installed, working heat source (no unvented space heaters) is required in HUD-designated climate zones; also hot and cold running water. Not visible in our data.
safe path from the unit door to the street; living room and each sleeping room need a window (HQS), and most PHAs want bedroom windows that open for escape.
no FEMA flood zone on record for this house
no warning signs in the exterior data we have (roof surface spread 12.5 cm), but no city code-case data for this house; interior condition unknown
